001 / CaveBusters Rover

Capstone SolidWorks Arduino 3D Print
CaveBusters — Autonomous Mine Rescue Rover
An autonomous mechanical rover designed for mine rescue missions. Features a custom CAD chassis, FDM printed structural links, 4WD differential drive, and Arduino ultrasonic sensor fusion.

Project Overview

The CaveBusters rover addresses mine site safety by mapping confined spaces autonomously. Its structural assembly protects onboard micro-controllers while aligning ultrasonic sensors to navigate blockages.

Physical Build Verification

Rover Prototype — 4-Axis Inspection

Build Steps

  1. 1
    Defined mission envelope: clearance parameters, suspension articulation, and component access portals.
  2. 2
    Modeled complete assembly in SolidWorks, verifying kinematic clearance on all steering joints.
  3. 3
    Printed FDM structural links in high-infill PLA, checking mechanical tolerances.
  4. 4
    Assembled drivetrain, motor mounts, and aligned three HC-SR04 sonar sensors.
  5. 5
    Programmed navigation state machine in Arduino IDE with obstacle escape logic.
  6. 6
    Tested steering calibration and wheel velocity control on simulated gravel paths.
  7. 7
    Compiled detailed draft sheets for peer engineering evaluation.

002 / CNC Mill Conversion
Drag · Scroll: Zoom · Right-drag: Pan
CAM Build SolidWorks CNC / GRBL Ender 3 V2
Compact CNC Mill — 3D Printer Conversion
A rigid desktop CNC mill built by modifying an Ender 3 V2 frame. Replaces rubber V-wheels with MGN12 linear rails and T8 leadscrews for machining aluminum stock.

Project Overview

This project converts an Ender 3 V2 into a milling tool, utilizing the frame while replacing linear carriages with MGN12 guide blocks to withstand mechanical cutting loads.

System Specs

Base Frame
Ender 3 V2
Linear Motion
MGN12 Linear Rails
Drive Assembly
T8 Leadscrews
Firmware
GRBL (CNC Shield)
Spindle Motor
Brushless 500W
Runout
< 0.02 mm

Build Steps

  1. 1
    Disassembled printer and checked frame squareness using dial indicators.
  2. 2
    Designed custom bracket adapters for MGN12 carriage blocks in SolidWorks.
  3. 3
    Mounted precision MGN12 rails on X, Y, and Z axes to remove V-wheel backlash.
  4. 4
    Assembled leadscrews and motor couplers, ensuring correct linear alignment.
  5. 5
    Wired CNC shield controller, adjusting GRBL steps/mm calibration parameters.
  6. 6
    Machined adapter plates from aluminum block, testing spindle deflection values.
  7. 7
    Executed profile cuts on soft timber and acrylic to optimize feed rates.
